llm.summary: This skill is a disclosed SocialEcho API helper; it can publish or sync live social/catalog data, but that behavior matches its stated purpose and is not hidden.

dimensions.detail: Network access is limited by the wrapper code to user-selected SocialEcho API base URLs, defaulting to https://api.socialecho.net, with bearer API-key authentication and no evidence of hidden local indexing or broad filesystem access.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: package.json declares bin/script entries and no dependencies or install lifecycle scripts such as preinstall, install, postinstall, or prepare.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions require an explicit --api-key and do not auto-read environment variables. The TikTok Shop sync command requires --execute, while publish-article is clearly named and requires a user-supplied payload file but does not add a separate confirmation or dry-run step.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No persistence, background worker, privilege escalation, credential harvesting, subprocess execution, or destructive local file mutation was found; file reads are limited to the supplied publish payload and bundled platform-limit markdown files.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The skill provides CLI wrappers for SocialEcho team, account, OAuth link, article, report, upload URL, Reddit/Pinterest lookup, TikTok Shop catalog/music, product sync, and cross-platform publishing APIs; the live publishing and sync capabilities are sensitive but purpose-aligned and disclosed in SKILL.md.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you intend to let the agent operate SocialEcho with a Team API key. Treat publish-article and tiktokshop-product-sync as live account actions: review payloads, target account IDs, schedules, and platform limits before running them, and keep the API key scoped and rotated according to your SocialEcho team practices.
llm.findings: [SQP-2] expected: The finding correctly points out that live publish and sync commands can affect third-party accounts, but the capability is disclosed and central to the skill. TikTok Shop sync has an explicit --execute gate; publish-article lacks a built-in confirmation/dry-run, so this is user guidance rather than a Review-level concern.
